title: Finite affine etale chart fibres imply quasi-compact field representatives
statement: Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $x\in|X|$ [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose there are a field $k$ [def-weil-field] and a monomorphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$ such that, for every affine scheme $U$ and every representable etale morphism $U\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], the scheme $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite over $k$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Monomorphism means injectivity on morphisms from every test scheme. Then every field-valued representative $\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ of $x$ is quasi-compact: for every affine scheme $T\to X$, with no etale hypothesis on this test, $T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme].

proof.text: Choose an etale atlas $\coprod_i U_i\to X$ with all $U_i$ affine, by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Put $F_i=U_i\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$. By hypothesis $F_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, hence affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; since the target is affine, $F_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2). Thus $F_i$ is quasi-compact and $U_i$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Consequently $F_i\to U_i$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). The empty $F_i$ is allowed. These conclusions concern the maps to $U_i$, not just the finite maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$.

The family $\{U_i\to X\}$ is jointly surjective and etale; on scheme tests its maps are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local] to this family and $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$, using step 1. The scheme and algebraic-space notions of quasi-compactness agree for these representable maps by the last sentence of [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. This proves that $j$ is quasi-compact. In particular its pullback over every affine scheme $T\to X$ has quasi-compact source, even when $T\to X$ is not etale.

Let $q:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ represent $x$. Set $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ with projections $a:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $b:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. This is a scheme: it is the pullback of the representable diagonal of $X$ along the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], equality of the point classes supplies a common field $\Omega$ and compatible maps from $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$; their pair defines a map to $Y$, so $Y$ is nonempty. For any scheme $H$, if two maps $H\to Y$ agree after $b$, their composites with $a$ agree after $j$ and hence agree, since $j$ is monic. The fibre-product property makes the two maps equal, so $b$ is monic. Apply [lem-sfb-monomorphism-into-field-coproduct] with a singleton indexing set: $Y$ is either empty or isomorphic over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ to $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Nonemptiness excludes the first case. Therefore $b$ is an isomorphism, and $h=a b^{-1}$ satisfies $q=jh$. This writes out the factorization of Stacks Tag 0H2X rather than assuming it.

Fix an arbitrary affine scheme $T\to X$ and write $F=T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$, $E=T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$. Both are schemes by the representable diagonal [def-trf-algebraic-space], as in step 3. Step 2 and [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] give quasi-compactness of $F$. The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is quasi-compact and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; hence $h:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). The equality $q=jh$ identifies $E$ with $F\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$: a map into either side is precisely a pair of maps into $T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L$ whose composites to $X$ agree, with the map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ forced by $h$. Thus $E\to F$ is a base change of $h$, so is quasi-compact by part (3) of that same permanence node. Since $F$ is quasi-compact, part (2) gives quasi-compactness of $E$. This proves the required assertion for every affine test $T$, without any etale or separation hypothesis on its map to $X$.

The statement is Stacks 03JV (3)=>(6) with S=Spec Z; I read the source and its full proof. Step 1: from a finite fibre to an affine F_i (finite-integral def, affine permanence (2)), then F_i->U_i is quasi-compact (qcqs node, permanence (1)). Step 2: the fppf-local descent applies to the affine etale atlas. Joint surjectivity comes from |w|, and representable etale gives flat and lfp. Scheme and space quasi-compactness agree by the last sentence of affine-tests; the space-test versus scheme-test difference is an elementary check. This gives j quasi-compact over every affine T. Step 3 writes out 0H2X correctly: Y=Spec k x_X Spec L is a scheme by the representable diagonal and is nonempty from the common-field point classes. b is monic because j is monic on test schemes, and 03DP with a singleton index (lem-sfb-monomorphism-into-field-coproduct) makes b an isomorphism, so q=jh. Step 4: E is isomorphic to F x_{Spec k} Spec L; h is quasi-compact by permanence (1) with no finiteness of L/k, then (3) and (2) give E quasi-compact. Tested on X=Spec k, on charts that miss x, and on an infinite extension L/k. No duplicate: the related 03JV nodes are (2)=>(6), (6)=>(4) and the quasi-separated case. No cycle and no SGA citation. lean.statement: theorem quasiCompact_field_representatives_of_finite_etale_chart_fibres (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (x : Point X.obj.obj) (K : Type u) [Field K] (b : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) (j : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj) (hj : schemePointMap j (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) (hmono : ∀ H : Over (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))), Function.Injective (fun a : yoneda.obj H ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ↦ a ≫ j)) (hfinite : ∀ (U : Over (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))), IsAffine U.left → ∀ a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj, IsEtale a → ∃ (V : Over (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (p : V ⟶ Over.mk b) (r : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj U), IsPullback r (yoneda.map p) a j ∧ IsFinite p.left) : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] (c : Spec (.of L) ⟶ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) (q : yoneda.obj (Over.mk c) ⟶ X.obj.obj), schemePointMap q (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x → ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))), IsAffine T.left → ∀ t : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X.obj.obj, ∃ (V : Over (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (p : V ⟶ T) (r : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk c)), IsPullback r (yoneda.map p) q t ∧ CompactSpace V.left
